description: DiggerLid PRO Excavator Enclosure 60s Meta ad — 11-frame storyboard.

frames.prompt:
RENDER MODE — STRICT BLACK AND WHITE PENCIL STORYBOARD SKETCH. The whole artwork is monochrome graphite + ink wash on warm cream sketchbook paper: loose hand-drawn pencil and marker lines, minimal shading, rough cinematic composition. Pencil tones only — no colour fills anywhere unless the [Visual] block below explicitly calls out a DiggerLid yellow accent. The cream paper is the only off-white. One frame from an 11-frame storyboard series for a 60-second ad.

[Context] Opening hero shot — the XE17U landing on a clean three-quarter hero. Conveys the rapid-fire shutter-click feel of the cut sequence in a single storyboard frame.
[Visual] A brand-new XCMG XE17U compact mini-excavator on a clean blank studio backdrop, photographed at a three-quarter angle, boom and bucket gracefully lowered, tracks square to camera. Factory-fresh, immaculate, every panel and decal crisp. Around the machine, four faint motion-streak rays radiate outward at varying angles — shutter-flash energy suggesting rapid-fire camera cuts. Small sketch-style burst marks at three or four points around the silhouette to read as "click moments". Empty white space dominates the rest of the frame.
[Format] 9:16 vertical, single composition.
[Style] B&W storyboard sketch on cream paper, loose pencil and marker lines, minimal shading, clean editorial composition. No colour anywhere. No text.

Persistent characters: Luke and Joel — the two DiggerLid founders, two real Australian tradesmen. Preserve their faces exactly from the reference portraits attached. LUKE = broad-shouldered build, neatly-trimmed dark moustache, ALWAYS wears a black baseball cap with the brim facing forward, dark hair just visible at the temples below the cap line. JOEL = slimmer build, distinctive thick full chevron moustache, mid-brown hair worn in a clean side part, NO cap, clean-shaven on the cheeks and chin.

[Context] Problem agitation — the machine takes the elements, then the punchline reveal: there's literally nothing to protect it with.
[Visual] A two-panel vertical split frame. TOP PANEL: the XCMG XE17U excavator standing alone outdoors, hammered by extreme weather — diagonal rain streaks, scattered hail-pellet dots, swirling wind lines, heavy storm clouds packed above, the cab fully exposed and unprotected. BOTTOM PANEL: a hard-cut moment of quiet — Luke (black cap, dark moustache) and Joel (chevron moustache, no cap) standing side-by-side over a flat-folded brown cardboard shipping box on a workshop bench, both staring DOWN into the empty interior of the box, expressions deadpan and dumbfounded. The box is clearly, comically empty — nothing inside.
[Format] 9:16 vertical, two stacked panels.
[Style] B&W storyboard sketch on cream paper. Top panel: dramatic weather, dynamic line work, kinetic. Bottom panel: still, deadpan, documentary. No colour, no text.

[Context] Villain reveal — the tarp solution fails in real time. Single dramatic action moment.
[Visual] The XCMG XE17U excavator parked outdoors, previously covered by a sagging olive-green canvas tarp held down with two black rubber ocky straps. CAUGHT MID-ACTION at the instant of failure: both ocky straps SNAPPED — the broken ends ricochet outward with motion lines and visible snap-back arcs at each end. The tarp itself is mid-air, peeled fully off the cab, twisted and partly folded, motion-blurred and lifted by a strong gust, exiting toward the upper-right of the frame in one continuous motion. Dust kicked up around the tracks, debris in the wind. The exposed cab beneath is now fully visible, tack-sharp.
[Format] 9:16 vertical, single composition.
[Style] B&W storyboard sketch on cream paper, dynamic action composition, motion blur on the tarp, sharp focus on the machine, kinetic snap-back lines on the broken straps. No colour, no text.

Descending from the upper edge of the frame, mid-air, the grey DiggerLid PRO Enclosure cover UNFURLING in slow motion onto the cab — caught at the moment it billows open like a parachute, edges rippling, the cover about to settle onto the cab. Heavenly god-rays of light stream down through atmospheric dust around the cover, lens-flare hint at the top of the frame. Around the cab, four DiggerLid-yellow tether points catch the light, glowing as the only coloured highlights — small but distinct. Reverent, cinematic, dust motes drifting in the rays.

[Context] Feature-dense montage — four hero specs in a tight grid. Cooling vent is referenced verbally in the VO and not granted its own panel; the four specs here are the most spec-credentialing macros.
[Visual] A clean 2x2 grid composition. TOP-LEFT: extreme macro of a black YKK side-release buckle mid-clip, embossed "YKK" letters legible on the buckle face, Luke's hand (with black cap visible at the edge of frame) holding the strap. TOP-RIGHT: the LEAR FRONT clear-PVC lower vision panel of the cover, unzipped and rolled up, with Joel (chevron moustache) visible behind it cutting a sheet of PVC at the workshop bench. BOTTOM-LEFT: macro of Luke's hand yanking a black UV-protected Velcro tab from grey ripstop fabric, fibres catching in motion. BOTTOM-RIGHT: interior cab POV looking down at a smartphone plugged into a black 12-volt accessory port on the dashboard, Luke's soldering iron just visible. Each panel a self-contained tight macro.

[Style] B&W storyboard sketch on cream paper, each panel a distinct feature-demonstration vignette, hyperreal sketch detail on hardware and fabric. No colour, no text — the "YKK" embossed letters on the buckle are the only legible mark in the frame.

BOTTOM PANEL: anamorphic-feel wide cinematic shot of a B-double semi-trailer truck driving along a long, dead-straight stretch of the Eyre Highway across the Nullarbor at dusk in heavy rain, tarp-covered freight on the trailers, wet bitumen reflecting the truck's lights, endless flat saltbush plain on both sides, sense of immense distance.

Each panel shows a different earthmoving operator using a digger or excavator fitted with a grey DiggerLid PRO Enclosure cover in adverse weather. Top row: pouring rain on a muddy worksite / snow falling on a Tasmanian mountain site / hail storm with ice pellets on the cover. Middle row: dusty drought-stricken farm / tropical Queensland monsoon downpour / outback dust storm with red-haze obscuring the machine outline. Bottom row: cold misty Snowy Mountains morning / sleet on Tasmanian bucket / golden-hour worksite after a storm cleared. Each panel has the candid raw look of a smartphone photo redrawn as a quick sketch — slightly imperfect framing, varied. Thin pencil-line gutters between panels.

[Style] B&W storyboard sketch on cream paper, each of the nine panels sketched in a candid UGC-style hand. No colour, no text, no watermarks.
